critiques.claim: Each requirement should be quantified, binding (client will pay for it), atomic, acceptable to all, and complete.
critiques.critique: 'Binding means client will pay' excludes legal, safety, regulatory, and ethical obligations. 'Acceptable to all' is impossible in genuine conflict. 'Complete' is an aspiration bounded by risk, not a provable state.
critiques.nuance: Desirable properties serve as quality targets, but strict adherence early on rejects valid exploratory needs.

extensions.title: Topic 9.3 Requirement Maturity & Uncertainty
extensions.summary: Maturity pipeline: Observed Need → Stated Req → Candidate → Accepted Obligation → Operationalized AC → Verified → Monitored Runtime.

fieldContext.note: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 provides standard requirement quality characteristics; a 3rd edition is currently in development.
